(7) For buildings that form part of the fixed assets and are let for consideration for residential purposes to persons who are not employees of the enterprise, the following shall apply with regard to repair expenses:
— Repair expenses that are incurred using correspondingly earmarked tax-free subsidies from public funds (Section 3(1) item 3, Section 3(1) item 5 subitems d and e, Section 3(1) item 6) shall, to that extent, be excluded from the profit determination.
— If, after offsetting the losses within the meaning of Section 11(1) item 3 determined without taking into account the repair expenses, tax-free reserves under Section 11 still exist, the repair expenses not covered by tax-free subsidies shall be offset against these tax-free reserves.
— Those repair expenses that were not covered by tax-free subsidies and were not to be offset against tax-free reserves shall be deducted in equal installments over ten years.

source_text:
For buildings serving residential purposes, the following applies with respect to repair and maintenance expenses: 
— Repair and maintenance expenses that are incurred using correspondingly earmarked tax-free subsidies from public funds are, to that extent, excluded from the determination of income. 
— If, after offsetting the losses determined without taking into account the repair and maintenance expenses within the meaning of Section 5(3), there remain tax-free amounts under Section 5, then the repair and maintenance expenses not covered by tax-free subsidies shall be offset against these tax-free amounts. 
— Those repair and maintenance expenses that were not covered by tax-free subsidies and were not required to be offset against tax-free amounts shall be deducted in equal instalments spread over ten years.

This does not apply as long as the sponsoring undertaking suspends the contribution payments (Section 4(4) no. 2 of the Income Tax Act 1988).
d) The pension commitments of the fund may not exceed 80% of the last current active remuneration.
e) The beneficiary must also have a legal entitlement to the pension upon termination of the employment relationship (vesting) if he/she has been a beneficiary for more than five years.
f) Upon termination of the employment relationship before the insured event occurs, the beneficiary's entitlements from own contributions and from employer contributions that have become vested may be settled or transferred to another pension fund.
g) After the insured event has occurred, the following may be settled:
— minor benefits and
— benefits for survivors' provision.
h) The entitled employees must have the right to participate in the administration of all amounts that flow to the fund.
